name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft on 12 Nov, still above the $4,000 Alert line
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft container on 12 Nov, led by lower transpacific and Asia–Europe rates, but stays above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Shanghai–New York fell 3% to $9,020, its lowest since August, and Shanghai–Rotterdam fell 3% to $3,504, while Shanghai port congestion rose to 49 hours from 36. Drewry expects transpacific rates to fall further but Asia–Europe rates to rise slightly in late November.
for_you: Importers and retailers shipping from Asia face container costs well above normal, which tends to feed through to shelf prices and delivery times over the following months.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
